the use of sentence level relevance feedback is an effective way to achieve high recall and that this method can be more efficient, relative to the use of document level relevance feedback, if the time and effort to review an entire sentence is less than that of an entire document.
the use of sentence level relevance feedback is an effective strategy for improving the efficiency of the CAL method.

the problem of high recall information retrieval and we present a novel simulation framework for evaluating active learning methods that use sentence level relevance feedback.

sentence level relevance feedback is a viable approach to improving recall in information retrieval, and that it is a particularly effective method for improving the performance of active learning algorithms.
isolated sentence feedback is a viable option that should be considered in future CAL research and development.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that sentence-based CAL is a promising direction for future work in the Total Recall track.
the use of sentence level relevance feedback can yield higher efficiency, relative accuracy, and comparable effectiveness, relative to the baseline BMI implementation of CAL.
sentence-level feedback is a good alternative to document-level feedback, and can be used in a CAL system without sacrificing performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of sentences for relevance feedback is a viable option for achieving high recall with active learning.
the use of sentences as units for relevance feedback can be more effective than full documents, and is an area of active research in the field of information retrieval.
, in the absence of a strong prior, it is reasonable to assume that isolated sentences are a more effective means of relevance feedback than the entire documents.
